name: android_tv_port_spec

decisions: Tier legend: 1 = pure Dart unit (crypto, DTOs, parsers, golden vectors, no I/O); 2 = protocol client against a fake transport/server in test; 3 = app-state/routing/storage with fakes; 4 = Android native (Kotlin) or UI. Priority P0 = needed for the local+cloud live-view MVP (sign-in -> list -> local or relay live view -> privacy/PTZ).

Windows behaviour is the reference where it differs from the TV baseline (appServerUrlV2, getAccountStatusAndUrl, -v2 IoT service id, common query params, thing-list roles). Baseline Topo code is kept only where it equals Windows.

Local control stack order of implementation: local_crypto (v3) -> camera_transport (TOFU pin) -> camera_control_client (login state machine + breaker) -> tpap (SPAKE2+ + CCM) -> LAT wiring. Live view on current C200-class firmware needs TPAP, so tpap is P0, not optional.

The TP-Link ID password cannot be dropped: the camera's local passcode (v3 secret, TPAP md5/sha256 candidates) and captchaLogin refresh need it. PORTING_BRIEF says 'never store the cloud password' -> proposal: store it only in Keystore-backed flutter_secure_storage, only after an explicit 'Keep me signed in' choice (default on for TV remote use, easy wipe on sign-out); LAT-only cameras and cloud-routed cameras work without it after sign-in (token + LAT). Needs the owner's approval.

SPAKE2+ and RSA-OAEP need a Dart crypto library (pointycastle or package:cryptography) because package:crypto has only hashes/HMAC. Run PBKDF2 (>=10k iterations x 80 B), RSA-2048 keygen and P-256 scalar mults in a background isolate; port the Windows BigInt affine arithmetic only as a fallback. Validate with the RFC 9383 vector before wiring to a camera.

Never test against real cameras. All local flows are tested against a Dart fake camera (port of tests/fixtures/mock_tapo_server: dispatcher, tpap_server, secure v3, legacy) and a fake cloud (port of tests/fixtures/mock_cloud.py). Golden vectors in this file are the byte-level gate.

Cloud-routed cameras (remote or shared) use the same DTO builders and the same ControlApi interface as LAN, with RemoteControlClient/CloudPassthrough as the transport (same pattern as Windows ControlApi).
Online state: IoT thing status==1 OR found by TDP; role from the thing record decides shared (role != 0).

Vector provenance: most vectors are copied from specs or tests in the Windows repo. Entries whose note says 'computed offline by the audit' were derived with hashlib/hmac/cryptography from the Windows test INPUTS (the tests assert the formula, not a literal); re-verify them against the Windows implementation when writing the Dart test.

TDP discovery uses dart:io RawDatagramSocket (broadcast) plus a MethodChannel for interface netmasks and a WifiManager MulticastLock when needed; no Kotlin crypto is required, all crypto stays in Dart.
Passwords, tokens, LATs, stok, keys: never in logs, toString, exceptions or test snapshots. Fake values only (test_password, 192.168.1.x).

decisions.decision: Dart terminates every protocol (Digest, Key-Exchange, AES/HKDF, multipart, relay TLS tunnel, acks, heartbeat, stop) and exposes only plain video/mp2t on the 127.0.0.1 RelayBridge with the per-launch key. No Kotlin networking, no ffmpeg. One MediaSource interface (local8800, relay, later vod) feeds the same bridge route /camera/<id>.ts.
Never forward JSON, audio/* or undecryptable parts to ExoPlayer: only video/mp2t bodies after HMAC check and decrypt; dropped bad parts do not end the stream (>50 consecutive does).

Audio: ExoPlayer/TsExtractor has no G.711 reader, so pcm_alaw (TS stream_type 0x90) is silently ignored and no remux inside TS can make it playable. P0 ships video only (volume 0). P2 adds a Dart TsAudioTap + A-law table decode + native AudioTrack for the focused camera, muted by default. AAC cameras play in ExoPlayer natively.

Per-camera limit 2 concurrent sessions via StreamLimiter keyed by camera id (local host or cloud deviceId); limit errors are fatal. Staggered start via existing StreamQueue (1 connecting at a time, 5 s slot timeout) extended to cover handshake and slot request.

Relay: align tunnel header order/set with Windows, add preview request, 15 s heartbeat, session_id acks (every 25th X-Data-Sequence), stop with 150 ms linger, 304 redirect follow (max 3), fresh slot per attempt. Encrypted relay parts stay unsupported (clear error) until a live capture defines the key schedule.

Keep LivePlayer.kt as is for P0: TS extractor flags, small LoadControl, 1.25x catch-up, TextureView non-focusable, emulator software-decoder preference. RTSP (P2) uses media3 RtspMediaSource natively, not the bridge.

Golden vectors for HKDF/MD5/HMAC/framing/A-law hex values were computed from the Windows implementation (python importing tapo_desktop read-only) because the Windows tests assert them structurally; the TV tests must pin these literals.

decisions: Tests live under test/widget_tv/ (Tier 3, flutter_test with tester.sendKeyDownEvent/sendKeyUpEvent/sendKeyRepeatEvent and LogicalKeyboardKey.*) and pure logic under test/unit/; the surface is fixed to 960x540 at devicePixelRatio 1.0.
Timeline direction keys: Left/Right scrub, Up = later day, Down = earlier day (matches the brief 'Up/Down day'); the date label shows the local day and is capped at tomorrow like Windows.
Menu/Info/Guide/F1 stay reserved for the remote guide everywhere (no screen may consume guideKeys); rename and other actions are reachable only through Hold OK menus and HUD buttons.
Sort, names, max remote streams are persisted in shared_preferences; camera account passwords only in flutter_secure_storage.
Saved grids keep the TV multi-preset model (id, name, layout, slots); Windows ViewLayout (25 slots, one global view) is not ported, only its dedup/unknown-id cleaning rules.
Local/Cloud badge derives from the control route chosen by the network lane (LAN found and role 0 = Local, otherwise Cloud); UI reads a Camera.route enum, tests inject it.
Siren and night vision tests use fake clients only; no test or demo build may switch real alarms (safety rules in PORTING_BRIEF).
README must gain a 'Using the remote' table generated from guide.dart rows; currently missing.

D1 P0 is SD playback of a chosen day: day list -> clip list (with -71103 fallback) -> one range get playback over :8800 (LAN) or relay streamType 1 (remote/shared) -> plain MPEG-TS to ExoPlayer through the loopback bridge. Seek = new range request (new relay slot when remote).

D2 Use only the verified request: scale 1/1, event_type [1,2], string times; speed is client-side pacing, so the TV needs a PTS-aware pacer between the camera and ExoPlayer (ExoPlayer cannot be trusted to pace faster-than-real-time TS). Pacing and position mapping live in Kotlin next to RelayBridge, with the pure PTS/timeline logic in Dart for Tier 1 tests, or fully in Kotlin with Kotlin unit tests (to decide in implementation).

D3 Motion notifications default to polling getLastAlarmInfo (5 s on LAN, 30 s cloud-routed); ONVIF PullPoint is optional and only when the user stores a camera account. No cloud push is used by Windows.

D4 Clip day window uses the TV's local timezone midnight; a day on the day list uses the camera's own dates, mismatch possible near midnight if the TV timezone differs from the camera's (open question).
D5 Download is out of scope for TV P0 (tier 4).
D6 Shared cameras (role 1) never log in locally and always go through relay VOD and cloud passthrough search.

items.title: Cloud request signing (Content-MD5 + X-Authorization HMAC-SHA1)
items.facts: Content-MD5 = base64(MD5(body)); empty body is sent AND hashed as '{}'. X-Authorization = 'Timestamp=9999999999, Nonce=<uuid4 lowercase>, AccessKey=<AK>, Signature=<hex lower HMAC-SHA1(SecretKey, md5+LF+9999999999+LF+nonce+LF+path)>'. path = encoded URL path only, incl. any regional path prefix, NO query, NO host. Timestamp is a constant. AK/SK are app constants (already in baseline tapo_cloud.dart). Body bytes = compact JSON UTF-8, no ASCII escaping; hash the exact bytes sent. IoT (services-sync, /v2/things) calls are NOT signed.

items.title: Common query parameters on signed account calls
items.facts: Every signed POST carries query: appName=TP-Link_Tapo_Android, appVer, netType=wifi, termID=<terminalUUID>, ospf='Android <rel>', brand=TPLINK, locale (xx_YY, default en_US), then token=<token> when the call needs it. items.title: Account API reply envelope and error mapping
items.facts: Reply = {errorCode:int, msg, result:{...}}. Effective code = envelope errorCode, else int(result.errorCode) (string in result). Non-JSON body -> malformed error. HTTP>=400 with code 0 -> HTTP error. Known codes: -20212 region redirect (result.appServerUrlV2), -20651 token expired, -20652 token mismatch, -20675 logged in elsewhere, -20677 MFA required (result.MFAProcessId + supportedMFATypes), -20601/-20615 wrong credentials (result.remainAttempts), -20661 locked (result.lockedMinutes), -20600 no account, -20602 not activated, -20676 bad MFA code, -23003 app too old. Response cap 16 MiB; timeout 15 s (login) .

items.title: TDP v2 probe packet (UDP 20002 and 20004)
items.facts: Packet = 16-byte big-endian header + compact JSON. Header: u8 version=2, u8 reserved=0, u16 opcode=1, u16 payloadLen, u8 flags (0x11 broadcast request = 0x10|0x01; 0x21 unicast), u8 ret=0, u32 serial (random < 2^28), u32 CRC32. CRC32 (IEEE/zlib) computed over the whole packet with bytes 12..15 set to 0x5A6B7C8D, result written big-endian at 12. Payload {"params":{"rsa_key":"<PEM SubjectPublicKeyInfo RSA-2048>"}} compact. One RSA key pair per process, reused. Send 3 probes 0.3 s apart to 255.255.255.255 and each interface directed broadcast, ports 20002 and 20004; collect replies for ~3 s from a socket bound to an ephemeral port with SO_BROADCAST.

items.title: TDP reply parsing and validation
items.facts: Replies may be concatenated: loop while >=16 bytes remain; len==0 or truncated -> stop; CRC mismatch (recompute with seed in slot) -> stop (framing unreliable); skip packet if version!=2, ret not in {0,1} or serial != probe serial. Payload JSON {error_code:0, result:{ip, mac, device_type, device_model, device_id (MD5 upper hex, may be present next to encrypt_info), encrypt_type:[..], tpap:{pake:[..],user_hash_type?,port?}, encrypt_info:{key,data}}}. error_code != 0 or missing result -> ignore. ip from result.ip (valid IPv4) else sender address. Identity: md5 = MD5(decrypted device_id) if encrypt_info decrypts, else top-level device_id lowercased if 32-hex, else ''. http_port from decrypted http_port, 0 or invalid -> null (default 443). Dedupe by normalised MAC (first wins). Never throw on hostile datagrams.

items.title: encrypt_info decryption (RSA-OAEP-SHA1 + AES-128-CBC)
items.facts: encrypt_info = {sym_schm:'AES', key:b64, data:b64}. key_iv = RSA-OAEP(MGF1-SHA1, hash SHA1, no label) decrypt of b64(key); need >=32 bytes: AES key = key_iv[0:16], CBC IV = key_iv[16:32]. data = b64 -> AES-128-CBC -> PKCS7 unpad -> UTF-8 JSON {device_id (40-hex full id), http_port, connect_ssid, connect_type, owner}. Any failure returns {} (identity then falls back to top-level md5). Dart needs an RSA lib (pointycastle) for keygen 2048 + OAEP-SHA1; key generation on a TV CPU can take seconds: generate once, off the UI isolate, cache in memory (PEM must be SPKI with 64-char lines + trailing LF per the app, Windows uses cryptography default PEM).

items.title: Cloud <-> LAN matching
items.facts: normalise_mac: strip [\s:.-], uppercase, must be 12 hex else '' ; output AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF. device_id_md5 = lowercase MD5 hex of the UTF-8 deviceId. Pass 1: map LAN devices by lowercased md5 (first wins) and assign to cloud devices by md5(deviceId). Pass 2: for unmatched cloud devices, match by normalised MAC among unused LAN devices. Each LAN device is used at most once; an md5 match always beats a MAC match; unmatched cloud devices are absent. Matched cameras get host=ip, https_port=http_port||443, lan_found=true, control_protocol 'tpap' when tpap_requested(raw.tpap, raw.encrypt_type).

items.title: Secure login (encrypt_type 3) hash primitives
items.facts: SHA256U = SHA-256 over UTF-8, UPPERCASE hex. MD5U = MD5 UPPERCASE hex. cnonce = 8 random bytes as 16 UPPERCASE hex chars. first_hash = SHA256U(cnonce + SHA256U(password) + nonce). expected device_confirm = first_hash + nonce + cnonce (camera proves it knows the password; compare constant-time against result.data.device_confirm BEFORE sending digest, no login attempt is spent). digest_passwd = SHA256U(SHA256U(password) + cnonce + nonce) + cnonce + nonce. In LAT mode the secret is the raw LAT instead of the password: try [LAT, password] against device_confirm and use whichever verifies.

items.title: Secure session keys, cipher, envelope and tag
items.facts: lsk = SHA256('lsk'+cnonce+nonce+first_hash)[0:16], ivb = SHA256('ivb'+cnonce+nonce+first_hash)[0:16] (raw bytes of the digest, first 16). Cipher AES-128-CBC/PKCS7 with fixed lsk/ivb; base64 standard padded, no newlines; decrypt validates base64, positive multiple of 16, padding, UTF-8 (errors are protocol errors => session invalid). Request = compact JSON (no spaces, no ASCII escaping, no \/ escaping) of inner dict, encrypted, wrapped as {"method":"securePassthrough","params":{"request":"<b64>"}} (exact string is hashed for the tag). Headers per request: seq=<n>, tapo_tag=SHA256U(SHA256U(SHA256U(password)+cnonce) + outerBody + str(seq)). seq starts at login start_seq and increments for EVERY attempt (consumed even if the request fails). POST /stok=<stok>/ds. Reply {error_code, result:{response:<b64>}} -> decrypt -> JSON.

items.title: Local login state machine (TPAP / secure v3 / legacy MD5)
items.facts: POST / with {"method":"login","params":{...}} (compact JSON). Step 1 (always): {cnonce, encrypt_type:'3', username:'admin'}. error_code -40211 -> TPAP (confirmed, no fallback). -40413 with result.data {nonce, device_confirm} -> secure v3 step 2 {cnonce, encrypt_type:'3', username, digest_passwd}; step 2 code!=0 -> auth error; result.stok + result.start_seq required. Anything else -> legacy {hashed:true, password:MD5U(password), username:'admin'}; result.stok; requests are then plain JSON on /stok=<stok>/ds without tag. If TDP hinted TPAP, skip step 1. If device_confirm matches neither LAT nor password: auth error WITHOUT sending digest. -40404/-40408 -> locked (result.data.sec_left seconds). HTTP 401 -> auth error, other non-200 -> protocol error. Session invalid on top-level or per-item -40401, securePassthrough -40210, HTTP 401: re-login once and retry once; second failure raises.

items.title: Local HTTPS transport: headers, TOFU pin, keep-alive
items.facts: HTTPS to host:https_port (443 or TDP http_port). Headers: Accept application/json, User-Agent 'Tapo CameraClient Android', requestByApp 'true', Referer 'https://host:port', Content-Type 'application/json; charset=UTF-8' (TPAP /ds: application/octet-stream both ways), keep-alive. Camera certs are self-signed: no chain validation (badCertificateCallback) but pin sha256(DER) of the leaf on first contact per host:port (TOFU) and fail with CertificateMismatch on change; persist pins. Reuse one connection; on stale socket (reset/EOF) reconnect and resend once; timeouts are NOT retried (10 s). Serialise requests per camera (one lock) so seq cannot desync.

items.title: Auth circuit breaker and lockout rules
items.facts: After a TapoAuthError (wrong password / device_confirm mismatch / TPAP refusal) further logins on that client fail fast with the same error for 120 s (auth_retry_after) or until reset_auth_backoff() (user re-entered password OR the camera's LAT changed => rebuild client). Lockout (-40404/-40408) is NOT breakered here: raised immediately with sec_left. TPAP: at most 2 pake_share attempts per login (MAX_ATTEMPTS=2); never loop credential variants; background callers (status poll, events) must not retry a failed login. items.title: SPAKE2+ (RFC 9383) prover on P-256 with SHA-256
items.facts: Suite SPAKE2+-P256-SHA256-HKDF-SHA256-HMAC-SHA256 (cipher_suites 1). w0,w1 = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(passcode UTF-8, dev_salt, iterations, 80 bytes): w0 = int(dk[0:40]) mod n, w1 = int(dk[40:80]) mod n. Context = SHA256('PAKE V1' || user_random || dev_random). Prover: x random in [1,n-1]; shareP = x*G + w0*M (uncompressed SEC1 65 B). Verifier share Y (dev_share) must be on the curve. z = x*(Y - w0*N), v = w1*(Y - w0*N). Transcript TT = for each of [context, idProver(empty), idVerifier(empty), M(uncomp), N(uncomp), shareP, shareV, Z, V] u64-LE length || bytes, then u64-LE 32 || w0(32 B big-endian). K_main = SHA256(TT). K_confirm = HKDF-SHA256(K_main, salt none, info 'ConfirmationKeys', 64): K_confirmP=first 32, K_confirmV=last 32. confirmP = HMAC-SHA256(K_confirmP, shareV) (sent as user_confirm); confirmV = HMAC-SHA256(K_confirmV, shareP) (must equal dev_confirm, constant-time compare; mismatch => auth error without retry). K_shared = HKDF-SHA256(K_main, none, 'SharedKey', 32). M = 02886e2f97ace46e55ba9dd7242579f2993b64e16ef3dcab95afd497333d8fa12f, N = 03d8bbd6c639c62937b04d997f38c3770719c629d7014d49a24b4f98baa1292b49 (compressed). Dart: implement with pointycastle ECCurve_secp256r1 (or BigInt affine like Windows); needs HKDF/HMAC/PBKDF2 (package:crypto has HMAC; PBKDF2 with 10k+ iterations of 80 bytes must run in an isolate).

items.title: TPAP /ds channel: AES-128-CCM framing
items.facts: key = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_shared, salt='tp-kdf-salt-aes128-key', info='tp-kdf-info-aes128-key', L=32)[0:16]; nonceBase = HKDF-SHA256(K_shared, salt 'tp-kdf-salt-aes128-iv', info 'tp-kdf-info-aes128-iv', L=32)[0:12]. nonce(seq) = nonceBase[0:8] || u32_be(seq). AES-CCM tag 16 B, no AAD. Request body = u32_be(seq) || ciphertext || tag, POST /stok=<stok>/ds, Content-Type and Accept application/octet-stream; first seq = start_seq, every attempt burns a seq. Reply body: first 4 bytes seq (reply's own) then ct||tag; nonce from that seq. Plaintext JSON replies (starts with '{' and parses with error_code) mean refusal: -40401,-40418,-40420,-40421,-2402 => session invalid (re-login once); other codes => device error and drop session. HTTP 401 => session invalid; other non-200 => protocol error. Decrypt failure => session invalid. Only 'aes_128_ccm' supported (pointycastle CCMBlockCipher/AESEngine or package:cryptography AesCcm).

items.title: Local :8800 handshake: unauthenticated POST, 401 Digest retry, Key-Exchange
items.facts: Open TCP (NODELAY) to <ip>:8800. Send 'POST /stream HTTP/1.1' with headers in order Host, Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=--client-stream-boundary--, Connection: keep-alive, Content-Length: 0, X-Key-Exchange: 1, then Authorization on retry. 401 -> parse WWW-Authenticate (realm, qop, nonce, opaque, algorithm, encrypt_type, userhash). If response Connection: close, reopen socket before retry. Secret = SHA256_HEX_UPPER(secret) when encrypt_type==3 else MD5_HEX_UPPER; secret is the LAT when known else the cloud password; empty -> default media password. Digest username admin, uri /stream, nc 00000001, qop first token, no spaces between fields. Second 401 -> auth failure, never retry (lockout rule). HTTP 503 / -52407 -> stream limit. After 200 read Key-Exchange header (space separated k=v, quotes stripped, nonce required).

items.title: HKDF stream keys, X-Nonce IV and X-Data-Hmac check
items.facts: Key-Exchange algorithm=HKDF (C200 fw 1.5.7): ikm = nonce + ':' + secret (secret = SHA256_HEX_UPPER of the LAT or password), salt = Key-Exchange 'salt' as UTF-8 bytes (None when empty), HKDF-SHA256 L=16, info 'stream_hkdf_aes_key' and 'stream_hkdf_hmac_key'. Per part: iv = hex-decode(X-Nonce) must be 16 bytes; X-Data-Hmac (optional) = base64(HMAC-SHA256(hmac_key, ciphertext)) compared in constant time; then AES-128-CBC PKCS7. Bad part is dropped (not fatal); >50 consecutive failures raise a broken-session error. Only parts with X-If-Encrypt: 1 are decrypted. Dart: package:cryptography or pointycastle (HKDF, AES-CBC); for 2-4 Mbit/s TS prefer a Kotlin MethodChannel/isolate only if Dart AES profiling shows >30% CPU on a TV box (open question).

items.title: Multipart framing: device parts in, client parts out
items.facts: Device boundary line on the wire is '--' + '--device-stream-boundary--' (four hyphens); client likewise '----client-stream-boundary--'. Parser: skip lines until one equals the delimiter, read header block to CRLFCRLF (latin-1, name: value), require numeric Content-Length (max part 16 MiB), then exactly that many body bytes; ignore blank/junk/closing lines; header block cap 64 KiB. Client parts: delimiter line, extra headers in insertion order, Content-Type, Content-Length, blank line, body, CRLF. JSON control bodies are compact (separators ',' ':'), seq starts at 1; X-Session-Id added automatically once known. The existing Dart parseRelayResponse uses containment matching and no pending-state buffering; replace it with a stateful MultipartReader shared by local and relay.

items.title: Preview request, session_id, acks, stop with linger
items.facts: After connect send {type:request,params:{method:get,preview:{channels:[0],resolutions:[HD|VGA],audio:[default]}}} (seq added = 1). HD = main stream, VGA = minor stream. Wait for type=response with matching seq (or none); result.error_code in {-52407,-52405,-52419,-52435} = fatal stream-limit, other non-zero = refused. Media parts (video/mp2t) that arrive before the response are kept (max 8) and replayed. session_id is read from params.session_id (real cameras) or result.session_id, or the X-Session-Id header; without it no ack/stop is sent. Ack every 25th X-Data-Sequence: part with X-Data-Received then X-Session-Id headers. Skip parts with Content-Type audio/*. End notifications: connection_closed, stream_finish, device_locked, internal_error; type=error ends the pump. Stop: send {type:request,params:{method:do,stop:null-string 'null'}} then wait 150 ms BEFORE closing the socket (Windows RST dropped the stop; apply the same linger on Android to be safe), then close. Backpressure: write to the HTTP response and await it; do not queue unboundedly. I/O timeout max(3 s, stall+1). Stall watchdog 5 s, backoff 0.5 s doubling to 10 s, TCP reachability probe 3 s before handshake.

items.title: Relay tunnel request: exact header order
items.facts: TLS to relayIp:443 (fallback relay host), SNI/hostname check = relay host from relayUrl, TCP_NODELAY, trust TP-Link roots plus system. Send one never-ending 'POST <relayPath>&retryTime=0 HTTP/1.1' (use ? if path has no query) with headers in this exact order: User-Agent 'Client=TP-Link_Tapo_Android Android <ver>/1.3', Keep-Relay 3600, Accept */*, Content-Type multipart/mixed;boundary=--client-stream-boundary--, Host, Content-Length 9223372036854775807, X-token, X-Client-Model, X-Client-UUID, X-Track-Id, X-Redirect-Times, X-Pull-Mode 2, [Cookie ELB], X-Version 2.0, X-Arrive-Latency (TCP connect ms). Missing X-Version gives 400 errorCode 3 illegal_request. Read the response head byte-by-byte so nothing after 200 is consumed. 200 -> raw tunnel. 304 -> body is RequestUrlResult, reconnect with X-Redirect-Times+1 (max 3). Other -> JSON errorCode/closeReason. TV baseline differs: Host first, no X-Track-Id, extra Connection: Keep-alive, X-Redirect-Times fixed at 0, Cookie placed last. Align to the Windows order and add 304 handling.

items.title: Relay media session: preview request, heartbeat every 15 s, plain TS
items.facts: Inside the tunnel there is no inner POST /stream and no Digest. The client writes the same preview request part as on LAN (resolution = slot resolution) and then reads device parts. items.title: ExoPlayer cannot play G.711 A-law inside MPEG-TS
items.facts: media3 DefaultTsPayloadReaderFactory creates payload readers only for stream types MPA 0x03/0x04, AAC ADTS 0x0F, AAC LATM 0x11, AC-3 0x81, E-AC-3 0x87, AC-4 0xAC, DTS 0x8A/0x82/0x88/0x8B, MPEG-2/H.263/H.264/H.265 video, ID3 0x15, SCTE 0x86, DVB subs 0x59. There is no G.711 reader; an unknown stream type (G.711 A-law is PMT stream_type 0x90 on Tapo cameras per pytapo/go2rtc) yields no track and the audio is silently dropped. So a camera TS with pcm_alaw plays video only and does not break playback. Remuxing inside TS cannot help because media3 has no PCM-in-TS reader either.

items.title: Audio design: Dart strips A-law PES, decodes to PCM16, plays via AudioTrack
items.facts: Phase 1 (P0): leave audio in the TS (ExoPlayer ignores it), player.volume stays 0, no work. Phase 2 (P1/P2): a TsAudioTap in Dart walks 188-byte TS packets, parses PAT/PMT, finds the audio PID (stream_type 0x90 = A-law, or 0x0F AAC which ExoPlayer plays natively with no tap), reassembles PES payloads (8 kHz mono, 1 byte per sample), decodes with the 256-entry A-law table to s16le and sends PCM chunks over a MethodChannel/EventChannel to a Kotlin AudioTrack (8000 Hz, mono, ENCODING_PCM_16BIT, MODE_STREAM, small buffer). The tap runs only for the focused/fullscreen camera and a mute toggle defaults to muted; sync with video is approximate (PTS offset) which is acceptable for monitoring. Alternative considered: have Kotlin MediaCodec 'audio/g711-alaw' decode - rejected because ExoPlayer still would not demux it from TS. Windows never decoded live audio (AGENTS.md: audio in live view not built); alaw.py is only a reference table.

items.title: Range playback request (get playback)
items.facts: One get playback request from the chosen start second to end_utc (normally end of the local day). Times are strings of UTC epoch seconds, start must be > 0, end >= start. client_id 1, channels [0], scale always '1/1' (only verified value), event_type [1,2] (timing + motion). seq is added by the session (incrementing from 1). Camera then plays the following recordings of the range one after another. Reply is type response with result {error_code, session_id, speed}; success is error_code 0 and a non-empty session_id; a missing session_id falls back to the media parts' X-Session-Id. Start/seek inside a gap snaps to the start of the next clip (to the requested time when no later clip).

items.title: SD playback over local :8800
items.facts: Same persistent POST /stream session as live view: Digest handshake, boundary --client-stream-boundary-- (client) and --device-stream-boundary-- (device), Key-Exchange (MD5 or HKDF keys, AES-128-CBC parts, X-Data-Hmac) as in the live-view lane. After connect send the get playback request. Device parts: video/mp2t (MPEG-TS, forward to the player) and application/json (notifications). Ack every 25 parts with the stream_sequence notification. Playback uses the cloud password or the local access token like live view; connection loss reconnects and resumes with a new request at the last position. Camera refusing with a non-zero error_code is fatal (no retry loop) to protect the camera.

items.title: SD playback through the cloud relay (remote/shared)
items.facts: Relay slot request with streamType 1 (playback; 3 is download, preview is live), channelId '0', customParams '{}', cloudType 2 (1 gives -1007). Tunnel is plaintext MPEG-TS parts with no inner POST /stream: first a get playback JSON part, then video/mp2t parts, ack every 25 parts, heartbeat every 15 s. Every start, seek or reconnect takes a NEW relay slot. The relay closes the tunnel after the last recording instead of sending 'finished'; treat position >= last clip end - 1.5 s as end. Verified on a real remote C510W (392 parts for a 66 s clip in 15 s). Stop request is do stop 'null'.

items.title: Pause, resume, seek, speed
items.facts: Pause: client holds the next frame, sends do pause 'null'. Resume: do play 'null'. If the camera dropped the paused connection the normal reconnect resumes from the last position. Seek = a fresh get playback at the new second (the in-session do play {start_time} seek is in the spec but unverified on real firmware); also resumes a paused playback and restarts after end of recordings. Speed: allowed 1/1, 2/1, 4/1, 8/1; the request always asks 1/1 and speed is applied client-side by pacing frames (limited by link throughput). Cameras send faster than real time while acked, so pacing by PTS is required.

items.title: Position tracking from TS PTS
items.facts: Recording time is derived from the video PES PTS (90 kHz, 33-bit wrap). Steps 0..3 s advance the position; a larger or backwards step means a new recording file and the position jumps to the start of the next clip of the day's list; running past a clip end + 1.5 s moves to the next clip start. Without a clip list and step < 86400 s the position advances anyway. Position callback about 5 times a second. Parts that are not whole 188-byte aligned TS packets are paced by the X-Data-PTS header. Needed so the TV can show a cursor on the 24 h timeline when ExoPlayer only sees a continuous TS.

items.title: End of recordings and notifications
items.facts: Camera notification stream_status status 'finished' ends the requested range. items.title: Motion notifications without a camera account: poll getLastAlarmInfo
items.facts: Windows tray notifications come from AppController.motion_event, fed by service.start_events. Choice: (1) cloud-routed camera (remote/shared): poll getLastAlarmInfo through cloud passthrough, interval max(5 s, 30 s) = 30 s; (2) LAN camera without a camera (third) account: poll getLastAlarmInfo over local HTTPS every 5 s; (3) LAN camera with a camera account: ONVIF PullPoint on :2020. No cloud/msg push is used. Poller: first reading is a baseline (no event); each later change of last_alarm_time emits one active event with type last_alarm_type (motion, person...); timestamp from last_alarm_time epoch string else now; topic 'tapo:LastAlarmInfo/<type or motion>'; source last_alarm_info. Errors are logged (1st, 10th, every 60th) and polling continues. Request is a plain control call with no secrets.

items.title: ONVIF PullPoint flow (only with a camera account)
items.facts: Port 2020, SOAP 1.2, POST with Content-Type application/soap+xml; charset=utf-8, one short connection per call, 8 MiB response cap. Steps: GetCapabilities (device service /onvif/device_service) to find the events XAddr path (fallback /onvif/service); CreatePullPointSubscription with InitialTerminationTime PT60S; SubscriptionReference/Address gives the path+query used for later calls and the wsa:To value; loop PullMessages (Timeout PT5S, MessageLimit 10, wsa:Action PullMessagesRequest) with a network timeout of pull timeout + socket timeout; Renew (wsnt:TerminationTime PT60S, Action RenewRequest) when the renew deadline passes (renew margin max(10 s, pull+net+2) capped at ttl/2); remaining ttl = TerminationTime - CurrentTime of the camera clock; Unsubscribe best effort (2 s) on stop or fault. Any failure re-subscribes with backoff doubling from 1 s up to 30 s. A callback exception must not stop the loop.

items.title: WS-Security UsernameToken digest
items.facts: Header Security (mustUnderstand=1) with UsernameToken: Username, Password Type=...#PasswordDigest = base64(sha1(nonce_raw + created_utf8 + password_utf8)), Nonce = base64(nonce) EncodingType Base64Binary, Created UTC 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'. Nonce is 16 random bytes per call. Plaintext password never appears in the XML. Password is the camera (third) account password, not the TP-Link ID password. Envelope is SOAP 1.2; SOAP Fault becomes a device error; HTTP 401 without SOAP body is an auth error. Camera clock skew can matter: Created uses the TV clock (open question).

decisions: Local plane = TDP + secure v3 / legacy MD5 / TPAP SPAKE2+ (LAT aware) on :443 and :8800 media; RTSP/ONVIF only with an optional per-camera camera account.
Remote/shared cameras: cloud passthrough for control, cloud relay (cloudType 2) for live and VOD.

Cloud password: not stored by default. Opt-in 'Remember password on this TV' stores it in Keystore-backed secure storage (needed for v3/TPAP password login and captchaLogin refresh). LAT cameras work without it.
Session/cloud tokens move from plain shared_preferences to flutter_secure_storage.
Every byte source reaches ExoPlayer as plain MPEG-TS on the 127.0.0.1 RelayBridge with a per-launch key; JSON/audio/bad-HMAC parts are never forwarded.
Audio: P0 video only. Later: Dart TS audio tap decodes G.711 A-law to PCM16 and plays it via a native AudioTrack for the focused camera, muted by default.
Per-camera limit of 2 media sessions; limit errors are fatal (no retry). StreamQueue keeps one connecting stream at a time.

Motion alerts without a camera account: poll getLastAlarmInfo every 5 s locally, every 30 s through passthrough; toast only (no live PiP, it would use a media session). ONVIF PullPoint only with a camera account.
Recordings open from a button in the live-view controls; speed menu inside the recordings player (OK shows controls).
Max remote streams: 1..8, default 4. Grid stays at most 3x3 on TV. The All-cameras grid follows the chosen sort order.
Camera account is per camera, as on Windows.
services-sync: use the thing's appServerUrlV2 with /v1 path like Windows; keep v2->v1 fallback harmless.
Crypto first in pure Dart (package:pointycastle / cryptography); move to Kotlin only if a Tier 4 measurement on a real TV box shows it is too slow.
